newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma urges halt to big monopolies reform.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma urges halt to big monopolies reform.

text.p: The communist-dominated lower house of the Russian parliament urged President Boris Yeltsin on Friday to suspend planned restructuring of major state-controlled monopolies.

Deputies, mostly from the opposition, voted 232 to nine in favour of a non-binding resolution to such effect, which named the RAO Gazprom natural gas group, the UES electricity network and the railways ministry as monopolies which needed defending.

Yeltsin reshuffled his government last month, scrapping some Soviet-style industrial management ministries and charging new First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov with restructuring the "natural monopolies", such as utilities and transport.

"We consider it is essential to suspend restructuring and reform, being implemented at the present time, of RAO Gazprom, RAO UES and the MPS (railways ministry), and henceforth proceed only on the basis of existing laws and to take account of public opinion when changing managers," the Duma resolution said.
Yeltsin vetoed a Duma bill passed earlier in the day that would have limited foreign ownership in UES to 25 percent and required the state to keep a 51 percent stake in the company.

"The processes of dismemberment and eventual privatisation of RAO Gazprom, RAO UES and the MPS, planned on the orders of the IMF in the interests of our Western competitors, will lead to a sharp decline in the efficiency of these sectors, and also to the undermining of Russia's economic and defence potential," the Duma said.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has made free market economic reforms an overall condition of credits to Moscow.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, whom Yeltsin has ordered to spearhead further reforms, has criticised the grip of big monopolies, especially in the energy sector.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is a former head of Gazprom and is seen as more sympathetic to large industrialists, though he recently told the Duma that monopolies required "fundamental reform".
